Fake Identity

By: Sasha OLD | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
What happens when your identity is stolen? Carte Blanche investigates a syndicate that have stolen the identities of victims in PE, only to try scam company's across the country out of millions.

Unique Selling Point:
Identity Thief Busted
As commonplace as identity fraud has become in South Africa, it’s rare to catch the perpetrators in the act. Operating in Johannesburg, a syndicate that has hijacked the identities of several victims country-wide and caused havoc for the companies they tried to defraud, gets the special Carte Blanche treatment as we track down the culprits and join the police in catching the ring-leader red-handed.



Summary:
WE WENT WITH THE JMPD AND ARRESTED THE SUSPECTS.

Script:


We investigated the impact of the critical shortage of rape and buccal swab kits across the country. More than 80% of police stations didn’t have any kits.Sexual assault evidence collection kits contain crucial tools to take samples from victims’ bodies…This evidence could mean the difference between a rapist getting away with it...or justice for the victim.

Thabo: There's units in the whole country that doesn't have any rape kits.Thabo -- which isn’t his real name... is part of the dedicated police unit trained to treat sexual assault victims sensitively. This unit is known as the Family Violence, Child Protection and Sexual Offences – or FCS.

Thabo T: We are struggling to get kits now for the past year, especially the buccal sample to compare the DNA that was found on the victim with a suspect.So with each and every suspect we use two buccal samples, one is for the comparison and the other one is for the confirmation.The shortage resulted in some victims having to wait 6 to 7 hours while the police officers try to source a kit from another station.

Claire Mawisa LINK I CANT IMAGINE WHAT IT MUST BE LIKE TO BE A RAPE VICTIM WAITING FOR ONE OF THESE PACKS IN THE PERPETRATORS BLOOD, SWEAT AND SEMEN, THE SECONDARY TRAUMA – UNIMAGINABLE.

Andrew: “In February this year we have 80 percent of our police stations with zero rape kits.DA Police Shadow Minister Andrew Whitfield explained that the tender to order rape kits had gone out three times and had not been approved, causing the delay.

Andrew: “There were two unsuccessful bids at one point, as well as one bid that ultimately was found successful but couldn't be awarded the tender because they were caught up in another corruption scandal.

UPDATE Following our story, media countrywide added their voices and put pressure on the police. Several Carte Blanche viewers got in touch, offering to donate kits. But because these contain very specific items selected by forensic experts, police were unable to accept donations. Penny Stein, one of our viewers, had visited a rape crisis centre last year -- so discovering the shortage of kits spurred her into action. Stein came up with another way of helping victims in their worst hour, by teaming up with the ANGEL NETWORK - a non-profit who want to help victims of rape.
so ive proposed donating R240,000 which will buy 2,000 fantastic comfort packs which include hygiene products...if we can give someone a second of dignity we’ve done our job.”
show packing of kits Angel Network board members - Sharon Lefkowitz and Hayley Glasser helped to pack them.

Sharon: “”our aim from the start has always been to help where help is needed by giving a hand up rather than giving a hand out.
Hailey Glasser - executive committee HG: “our aim is to double our initial donation...by donating comfort packs of R120.”


SHOW FINALLY sign
Police statement graphic After five days of intense media focus SAPS spokesman Vish Naidoo issued a statement announcing that a RAPE KIT SUPPLIER had finally been appointed. The contract will supply 13 different types of evidence collection kits – including adult and pediatric sexual assault kits, as well as buccal swab kits.

Vincentia Dlamini: 27.50 “We know DNA doesn’t lie, and if we do not have tools to actually collect that evidence is pointless, because now we are not going to have the proper evidence that cannot be disputed by the accused.”

WOMEN & MEN AGAINST CHILD ABUSE Operations Director of Women and Men against child abuse Vincentia Dlamini says the lack of kits in recent years/months had made her job as a forensic nurse - impossible.

Vincentia Dlamini VD: “How is this going to be managed, because in.an area where there are only 2 rape cases in a week, 20 crime kits, and give the same number of crime kits to an area where 200 women raped...so there needs to be proper distribution of where there is a need for those crime kits.”
